title: Captive portal "Log in" opens the connectivity check URL over HTTPS instead of the portal login page
line: "Log in" on a captive portal network (notification, Networks banner and tray menu) now opens the portal's login page instead of a browser error.
explanation: All three "Log in" actions opened NetworkManager's connectivity check URI (on Fedora http://fedoraproject.org/static/hotspot.txt) in the browser. Browsers upgrade it to HTTPS when the domain is HSTS-preloaded or HTTPS-only mode is on, and a captive portal can only intercept plain HTTP, so the user got "This site can't provide a secure connection" and never saw the portal. Now plasma-nm requests the check URI itself without following redirects and opens the http(s) page the portal redirects it to; if there is no such redirect (no portal, error, 5 s timeout, non-web URL) it opens the check URI as before.

commits.message:
captive portal: open the portal's login page, not the check URI

Log in opened the connectivity check URI, which browsers upgrade to
HTTPS with HSTS or HTTPS-only mode, so the portal could never redirect
it. Fetch the URI ourselves and open the page the portal redirects to.

BUG: 527387

media.caption: Master: notification's Log in opens http://fedoraproject.org:8087/static/hotspot.txt, Chrome upgrades it to HTTPS (HSTS preload) and shows ERR_SSL_PROTOCOL_ERROR; the fake portal never gets a request
Fix: the same Log in opens http://127.0.0.1:8087/login, the fake portal's login page
Master: the Networks applet's "You need to log in to this network" Log in button, same SSL error
Fix: the applet's Log in button opens the portal login page

review.text: The small redirect-lookup approach in plasma-nm is the right direction and covers all three captive-portal 'Log in' entry points while restricting redirects to http/https with fallback to the check URI. However, libs/captiveportal.cpp uses a process-lifetime static QNetworkAccessManager with default cookie jar and connection pooling, so untrusted captive portals can persist cookies on the intercepted check host or leave stale pooled connections across network changes in long-lived kded6 and plasmashell processes. In addition, checkUrl and RedirectionTargetAttribute should be validated explicitly, and NetworkStatus::openNetworkLoginPage() drops Wayland XDG activation token propagation before the async fetch.
changes: In libs/captiveportal.cpp, avoid persisting cookies or pooling stale connections across untrusted networks in a static QNetworkAccessManager: either create a per-request QNetworkAccessManager deleted on reply finish, or explicitly disable cookie load/save (QNetworkRequest::CookieLoadControlAttribute / CookieSaveControlAttribute = Manual) and clear/disable connection reuse.

Validate checkUrl.isValid() before issuing the request, and explicitly check the RedirectionTargetAttribute QUrl with redirect.isValid() and target.isValid() rather than relying on checkUrl.resolved(QUrl()) == checkUrl.

In NetworkStatus::openNetworkLoginPage(), request an XDG activation token (e.g. via KWaylandExtras::requestXdgActivationToken) before starting the async HTTP fetch so raising an already-open browser works reliably on Wayland (especially from the tray context menu, which closes immediately on click).

reviews.text: The diagnosis is right and the redirect-lookup approach is sound: all three Log in entry points now fetch the check URI themselves without following redirects and open the http(s) target, falling back to the old behaviour, and the rig evidence (fake portal, HSTS-upgraded check URI, before/after for notification and banner) proves it. But the reporter already has MR !689 open for this bug, whose first version was this same redirect lookup with tests; a parallel, test-less MR is not how a maintainer will want this to land. Also, clicking Log in can now do nothing visible for up to 5 s while the lookup runs, and the applet paths open the browser without an activation token.
changes: Coordinate with MR !689 (comment there proposing to go back to the small redirect-lookup version, or co-author) instead of opening a competing MR
Add the autotest from !689's first version (or an equivalent QNetworkAccessManager/local server test) for redirect, no-redirect and non-http targets
Shorten the timeout (e.g. 2-3 s) or give feedback while waiting, and pass an xdg activation token on the applet paths too
Put the commit message in repos[0].commit in entry.json like the other entries
